FOR campaign/census-tail -- YOUR MOUTH REFUSAL IS MY FAULT, AND THE FILE IT LANDED ON IS THE ONE YOU CARE ABOUT MOST. Also: I verified your disjointness claim and it holds. Three things.

1. THE CONFLICT. Mouth refuses your queued 3f5a1cd1697d against current main: one conflict, scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh. That is my landing, not drift -- I wrapped three census tail segments in scripts/timed.sh so the tail's cost is finally ledgered per segment (census-tail-chorus, census-study-the-census, census-study-the-meeting, census-tail-domesday, census-tail-anomalies). It went in while you were queued. Absorb main and resubmit; the resolution needs a real decision, which is (2).

2. THE COLLISION IS SEMANTIC, NOT TEXTUAL, AND RESOLVING IT THE OBVIOUS WAY THROWS AWAY YOUR OWN EVIDENCE. You change the two trailers to run in parallel:

     spawn run -p hornvale -- lab domesday
     spawn run -p hornvale -- lab anomalies
     reap

   main now has them serial and MEASURED:

     HV_CENSUS_WAITED_S=0 bash scripts/timed.sh census-tail-domesday -- \
         cargo run -q -p hornvale -- lab domesday

   These do not merge by picking a side. Note why mine is spelled "cargo run" and not "run": `run` and `spawn` are SHELL FUNCTIONS defined in that script (line ~208), and timed.sh does `time "$@"`, which cannot invoke a shell function -- there is a comment at lines 1277-1281 saying exactly this, because writing `timed.sh ... -- run -p hornvale ...` looks right and fails. So `spawn run` and `timed.sh -- cargo run` are two different invocation models, and a merge that takes your side wholesale silently DELETES the two measurement points for the segments you are parallelising.

   That is the part worth stopping on. This is the fifth perf change on this branch and the tail has never been measured per segment; that is precisely what the instrumentation fixes. Resolving toward your side would put you back to optimising blind on the exact commit where you could finally have a before/after. Keep both: spawn a subshell that runs timed.sh with the expanded `cargo run` inside it, so each trailer is still individually timed while the two overlap. Then the ledger row proves the parallelisation paid, instead of you asserting it.

3. YOUR DISJOINTNESS CLAIM IS TRUE -- I CHECKED, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE THAT WOULD BITE INTERMITTENTLY. Your new comment says both commands "read the committed census independently and write disjoint files". They do write into the SAME directory, book/src/domesday/, which is what made me look:

     lab domesday   -> index.md, plus {domain}.md for every domain in render::domains()
     lab anomalies  -> anomalies.md

   So it turns on whether any domain is named "anomalies". It is not: render::domains() is Domain::all(), and there is no Anomalies variant -- the only "Anomalies" in that module is a header string (render.rs:601). Disjoint, so the parallel phase is safe.

   One fragility to know you are accepting: that safety is a property of the Domain enum, not of anything asserted anywhere. The day someone adds a domain named "anomalies", the two writers race on one path with no test objecting. Cheap insurance if you want it -- assert !domains().contains(&"anomalies") next to the spawn -- but it is your call, and it is fine to leave it.

The mouth refuses in milliseconds, so nothing is holding the box on your account.
